record.context_brief: Perturbations, weak-gap closeness, and stability of Krylov solvability
record.original_question: Consider a perturbation A~ f~ = g~ of an inverse problem Af = g induced by a Friedrichs operator A, where A~ is close to A and g~ is close to g in a suitable sense. Determine when the Krylov subspaces K(A, g) and K(A~, g~) stay close in the weak-gap metric dbw on closed subspaces of a separable Hilbert space, when such perturbations preserve Krylov solvability, when they destroy or create it, and what additional conclusions hold when the perturbation also preserves the Friedrichs character of the operator.

evidence.quote: In a perturbative perspective, it is relevant to compare the possibly 'close' Krylov subspaces K(A, g) and K(A~, g~). A promising tool is the weak gap metric between subspaces of separable Hilbert space, inspired to the standard norm gap distance.

QUESTION 6: Consider a perturbation A~f~ = g~ of the inverse linear problem Af = g induced by a Friedrichs operator A, where in some suitable sense A~ ∼ A and g~ ∼ g. When, in the dbw-sense (Section 2.4), are the Krylov subspaces K(A, g) and K(A~, g~) close ? When does the perturbation preserve or alter the Krylov solvability of the problem ? What is the answer to the above questions when, in particular, the perturbation preserves the Friedrichs character of the linear operator ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a separable complex Hilbert space and let $A:\mathcal{D}(A)\subseteq\mathcal{H}\to\mathcal{H}$ be a densely defined linear operator of Friedrichs type (i.e., $A$ admits a symmetric restriction whose closure is self-adjoint, together with a positivity/boundary structure characteristic of Friedrichs operators). Given $g\in\mathcal{H}$ in the range of $A$, consider the inverse linear problem $Af=g$ and its associated Krylov subspace
$$\mathcal{K}(A,g):=\overline{\mathrm{span}}\{g,Ag,A^2 g,\dots\}\subseteq\mathcal{H},$$
provided $g\in\bigcap_{n\geq 0}\mathcal{D}(A^n)$. Recall that the problem is said to be Krylov-solvable if it admits a solution lying in $\mathcal{K}(A,g)$.

On the set $\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H})$ of closed subspaces of $\mathcal{H}$, define the weak-gap metric $d_{\widehat{bw}}$ as the Hausdorff distance, with respect to a metric inducing the weak topology on the closed unit ball of $\mathcal{H}$, between the closed unit balls of the two subspaces.

Suppose $\widetilde{A}$ and $\widetilde{g}$ form a "perturbation" of $(A,g)$ in the sense that $\widetilde{A}$ is close to $A$ (in a resolvent, graph, or strong/norm sense to be specified) and $\widetilde{g}$ is close to $g$ in $\mathcal{H}$.

Answer the following:
(a) Give verifiable conditions on the perturbation under which $d_{\widehat{bw}}(\mathcal{K}(A,g),\mathcal{K}(\widetilde{A},\widetilde{g}))\to 0$ as the perturbation tends to zero.
(b) Determine under which such conditions Krylov solvability of $Af=g$ is preserved by the perturbation, and identify mechanisms by which the perturbation can destroy Krylov solvability or create it where it was absent.
(c) Establish the sharper conclusions that hold when, in addition, $\widetilde{A}$ remains an operator of Friedrichs type.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the recent literature on Krylov solvability of Friedrichs systems. Partial results exist on Krylov subspace stability in the weak-gap metric and on persistence/gain/loss of Krylov solvability under perturbations of abstract inverse linear problems (works by Caruso–Michelangeli), but the specific combined question for Friedrichs operators—including the case where the perturbation preserves the Friedrichs character—has not been settled.

status_evidence.title: Open problems and perspectives on solving Friedrichs systems by Krylov approximation
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open questions concerning weak-gap closeness of Krylov subspaces and stability of Krylov solvability under perturbations of Friedrichs operators.
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly formulated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Krylov solvability under perturbations of abstract inverse linear problems
status_evidence.snippet: Studies persistence, gain, or loss of Krylov solvability under small perturbations using the weak-gap metric.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results on perturbative Krylov solvability exist but do not specifically resolve the Friedrichs case.

status_evidence.title: Structural properties of Krylov subspaces, Krylov solvability, and applications to unbounded self-adjoint operators
status_evidence.snippet: Develops weak-gap convergence results for Krylov subspaces of unbounded self-adjoint operators.
status_evidence.claim: Related stability results exist for self-adjoint operators, motivating but not solving the Friedrichs question.
